summary: Feed s159_double is degraded: 34.6% of TCP sessions are one-way and 14.7% of frames are sliced to ~192 bytes. NDR requires bidirectional traffic and full payload for TCP reassembly and detection, both are currently impaired.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker is delivering only one direction per TCP session to this NDR port. Most likely asymmetric routing with separate ingress TAPs/SPANs not aggregated, or a hash-based load-balancing rule splitting client->server and server->client to different tool ports.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR needs both directions (needs_both_directions=true). With 47/136 sessions (34.6%) one-way, TCP stream reassembly, session state tracking, and anomaly/beacon detection will fail or generate false positives/negatives.

recommended_fix.why: Aggregate both directions of each flow to the same NDR tool port using symmetric 5-tuple hashing so the NDR sees complete sessions for stateful analysis.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker slicing/snaplen is enabled and truncating frames to ~192 bytes, likely to save bandwidth or fit tool capacity. 264/1792 frames (14.7%) are cut short.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR needs full payload (needs_full_payload=true) for deep packet inspection, signature matching, and payload-based detection. Slicing removes L7 content and breaks detection coverage.

recommended_fix.why: Disable slicing / set snaplen to tool max 9216 bytes so NDR receives complete frames and full payload for analysis.
